summary: Benefits your employer provides other than in money are salary too, and are taxed at a value the rules set. Accommodation is valued at a share of your salary that depends on the size of the city, or on what the employer pays for a lease or a hotel if that is lower, less any rent you pay, plus a share of the cost of any furniture. This applies in both regimes.

routes.name: Accommodation from your employer
routes.description: A home the government provides at its licence fee, or one your employer owns, leases or books in a hotel, valued at a share of your salary for the time you lived there, less the rent you paid; a home your employer owns or leases and has given you since an earlier year is capped at the first year's value, raised with the cost inflation index.

routes.name: Furniture in the accommodation
routes.description: A share of the cost of furniture each year, or the hire charges if it is hired, less what you pay for it.

routes.name: Medical treatment abroad
routes.description: Your employer's spending on treatment, stay and travel abroad for you or your family, and one attendant, is not taxed as far as the Reserve Bank of India permitted the treatment and stay, and the travel is not taxed only if your income before it is not above a limit.

routes.name: Motor car
routes.description: A car your employer owns or hires, valued at a fixed amount a month by engine size, or at its running cost if it is only for your private use, and taxed only if you are a director, hold a substantial interest in the company, or your salary in money is above a limit; and the running of your own car or other vehicle paid by your employer, less an amount for official use.

routes.name: Services, utilities and education
routes.description: Household staff, gas, electricity and water, and your children's education paid by your employer.

routes.name: Meals and gifts
routes.description: Food your employer provides, taxed only beyond a limit per meal at work or by voucher, and not at all for tea or snacks or at a remote site; and gifts, vouchers or tokens from your employer, not taxed while their total in the year stays below a limit, and taxed in full once it reaches it.

routes.name: Loans and other benefits
routes.description: Interest-free or cheap loans, holidays, credit cards, clubs, and the use or transfer of your employer's assets.
